gitCommit.subject: Open the legal docs in-app instead of handing them to a browser
gitCommit.body:
Open the legal docs in-app instead of handing them to a browser

Three users hit "Unable to open URL: https://vitt.io/legal/terms" on the signup
screen and saw nothing happen at all. Both legal URLs return 200, so the link
was never broken: Linking.openURL asks iOS to hand the URL to an external
browser and rejects when the device has none available, which is what Screen
Time restrictions and MDM profiles produce. There was no .catch, so the failure
surfaced only as an unhandled rejection in Sentry.

consent.tsx already did this correctly, deriving its URLs from
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL and opening them with WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync, and has
never errored. Signup was the odd one out twice over: it used the apex host and
the external browser. That logic now lives in src/utils/legal.ts, which both
screens share, with a visible alert if the in-app browser also fails.

EXPO_PUBLIC_TERMS_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL are gone. They were set in
.env.example only and in no eas.json profile, so every shipped build took the
hardcoded apex fallback -- an indirection that was correct in development and
nowhere else.

Verified on the simulator: the terms open in an in-app sheet from app.vitt.io.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
